case_name: In Re APPLICATION OF ENBRIDGE ENERGY TO REPLACE AND RELOCATE LINE 5

issues.label: PSC subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must confirm PSC had statutory authority to approve this pipeline construction.

issues.label: Scope of PSC approval power
issues.why: Court must determine what aspects of the tunnel/pipeline project PSC may lawfully regulate or approve.

issues.label: Applicable statutory framework
issues.why: Court must identify which statutes govern (e.g., PSC enabling laws, 2018 PA 359/MSCA, NREPA/MEPA) and how they interact.

issues.label: Standard of judicial review
issues.why: Court must apply the correct deference and review standards for PSC decisions (lawfulness, reasonableness, evidentiary support).

issues.label: Preservation of issues
issues.why: Court must decide which arguments were properly raised before the PSC/COA and are preserved for further review.

issues.label: Standing of each appellant
issues.why: Court must determine whether each Tribe/party has standing (injury, causation, redressability; statutory standing).

issues.label: Ripeness and finality
issues.why: Court must assess whether the PSC order is final and the issues are fit for review given other pending permits/approvals.

issues.label: Mootness
issues.why: Court must check whether subsequent events or project changes moot any challenges.

issues.label: Exhaustion of remedies
issues.why: Court must decide whether appellants were required to exhaust administrative processes before judicial relief.

issues.label: Proper parties and intervention
issues.why: Court must ensure all necessary parties were included and interventions were properly allowed or denied.

issues.label: Administrative record adequacy
issues.why: Court must confirm the record is complete and supports review of the PSC’s findings and conclusions.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: Court must verify the PSC placed the correct burden (e.g., preponderance) on Enbridge for required showings.

issues.label: Evidentiary sufficiency
issues.why: Court must determine whether substantial/competent evidence supports PSC factual findings (need, safety, impacts).

issues.label: Arbitrary-and-capricious review
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC’s decisionmaking was rational, consistent, and explained.

issues.label: Reasoned explanation requirement
issues.why: Court must assess whether PSC adequately addressed material objections and alternatives.

issues.label: Due process in PSC proceedings
issues.why: Court must ensure notice, opportunity to be heard, cross-examination, and impartial decisionmaker requirements were satisfied.

issues.label: Ex parte communications issues
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether improper contacts or political influence tainted the PSC adjudication.

issues.label: Bias or prejudgment claims
issues.why: Court must address any allegations PSC commissioners prejudged issues or had conflicts.

issues.label: Compliance with APA procedures
issues.why: Court must determine whether the contested-case process complied with Michigan administrative law requirements.

issues.label: Interpretation of 1953 PSC precedent
issues.why: Court must decide what legal significance the 1953 approval and Lakehead v Dehn have for current authority/need.

issues.label: Collateral estoppel/res judicata
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether prior litigation precludes relitigation of certain issues or whether this is a new cause of action.

issues.label: Effect of constitutional changes
issues.why: Court must consider how Const 1963 art 4 §52 affects analysis compared to pre-1963 approvals.

issues.label: MEPA applicability to PSC action
issues.why: Court must decide whether MEPA/NREPA environmental duties apply to PSC approvals and in what manner.

issues.label: MEPA ‘feasible alternatives’
issues.why: Court must assess whether the agency/record considered feasible and prudent alternatives (including shutdown/other transport).

issues.label: MEPA ‘likely pollution’ standard
issues.why: Court must determine whether the project is likely to pollute, impair, or destroy natural resources and what proof is required.

issues.label: Public trust doctrine duties
issues.why: Court must evaluate state duties regarding Great Lakes/Straits resources and whether approvals comply with those duties.

issues.label: Great Lakes protections statutes
issues.why: Court must consider any Great Lakes Submerged Lands/related provisions affecting use of the lakebed/Straits.

issues.label: Tribal treaty rights scope
issues.why: Court must determine the nature and extent of asserted treaty fishing and usufructuary rights implicated by spill risk or construction.

issues.label: Duty to consider tribal impacts
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC/DNR/MSCA had to evaluate impacts on treaty rights and cultural resources and whether they did so.

issues.label: Federal preemption (pipeline safety)
issues.why: Court must assess whether federal pipeline safety law preempts state regulation of design/operation/safety conditions.

issues.label: Federal energy/commerce preemption
issues.why: Court must consider whether the Commerce Clause or federal energy regulation constrains Michigan’s ability to condition/deny approvals.

issues.label: International/foreign commerce effects
issues.why: Court must consider implications of a line largely serving Canada and whether that affects state authority or public-use findings.

issues.label: Eminent domain/public use nexus
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether the replacement serves a public use/benefit in Michigan relevant to regulatory approvals and any property-rights grants.

issues.label: Need and public interest finding
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC was required to find and did find public need/benefit for the replacement segment.

issues.label: Safety and risk assessment
issues.why: Court must determine whether PSC properly evaluated spill probability, consequences, and mitigation (including anchor strike risks).

issues.label: Comparative risk: tunnel vs existing
issues.why: Court must assess whether evidence supports PSC’s conclusion that the tunnel materially reduces risk compared to dual lines.

issues.label: Construction impacts evaluation
issues.why: Court must address whether temporary construction impacts to the Straits ecosystem were adequately considered and conditioned.

issues.label: Operation and maintenance oversight
issues.why: Court must determine what operational conditions PSC could impose and whether conditions are enforceable.

issues.label: Emergency response planning
issues.why: Court must decide whether spill response readiness was required as part of approval and adequately supported.

issues.label: Climate/GHG considerations
issues.why: Court must consider whether Michigan law required evaluating greenhouse gas or climate impacts from continued hydrocarbon transport.

issues.label: Segmentation and cumulative impacts
issues.why: Court must address whether the project was improperly segmented from broader Line 5 system impacts or related actions.

issues.label: Third-party utilities in tunnel
issues.why: Court must review PSC’s denial of co-location approval and whether it was within PSC authority and supported by evidence.

issues.label: MSCA statutory authority limits
issues.why: Court must interpret 2018 PA 359 to determine MSCA’s powers and constraints relevant to the tunnel lease/easement structure.

issues.label: Validity of MSCA-DNR easement
issues.why: Court must consider whether the DNR’s easement to MSCA was lawful and whether PSC could rely on it.

issues.label: Validity of 99-year lease plan
issues.why: Court must assess whether the lease arrangement is authorized, consistent with public trust limits, and affects PSC approval.

issues.label: Separation of powers concerns
issues.why: Court must consider whether PSC’s action improperly intrudes on executive/legislative responsibilities for Great Lakes resources.

issues.label: Contractual commitments effect
issues.why: Court must decide what legal weight to give Enbridge–State/MSCA agreements in the PSC’s public-interest determination.

issues.label: Agency reliance on future permits
issues.why: Court must assess whether PSC unlawfully approved contingent on permits/rights not yet secured or inadequately assured.

issues.label: Coordination with other regulators
issues.why: Court must consider interactions with DNR, EGLE, USACE, PHMSA, and whether PSC duplicated/omitted required analyses.

issues.label: Environmental justice considerations
issues.why: Court must decide whether disparate impacts (including on Tribes) required assessment under state law or agency policy.

issues.label: Remedy scope if error found
issues.why: Court must determine appropriate relief (vacatur, remand, injunction, conditions) consistent with administrative review limits.

issues.label: Stay/injunction standards
issues.why: Court must address standards for halting construction pending review, if requested.

issues.label: Harmless error doctrine
issues.why: Court must decide whether any procedural/substantive errors require reversal or are harmless on this record.

issues.label: Severability of PSC determinations
issues.why: Court must determine whether portions of PSC order (e.g., utility co-location denial/approval conditions) can be severed.

issues.label: Compliance with Michigan Constitution art 4 §52
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether state actions adequately ‘provide for’ protection of natural resources as a constitutional constraint.

issues.label: Interpretation of ‘reasonable and safe’
issues.why: Court must define and apply the correct legal meaning of statutory/administrative standards like ‘reasonable,’ ‘safe,’ and ‘public interest.’

issues.label: Adequacy of findings of fact
issues.why: Court must determine whether PSC’s written order contains sufficient factual findings to permit meaningful appellate review.

issues.label: Consideration of alternatives: shutdown
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC had to consider decommissioning without replacement as an alternative and how it weighs.

issues.label: Consideration of alternatives: reroute
issues.why: Court must assess whether non-Straits routing options were feasible alternatives requiring evaluation.

issues.label: Consideration of alternatives: rail/truck
issues.why: Court must address whether other transportation modes were feasible/prudent alternatives under MEPA or public-interest review.

issues.label: Economic impacts and benefits
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether PSC appropriately weighed energy supply reliability, propane availability, and economic effects.

issues.label: Reliance interests and transition
issues.why: Court must consider reliance by consumers/industries (UP propane, airport fuel) and transition feasibility in balancing harms.

issues.label: Jurisdiction over Canadian deliveries
issues.why: Court must determine how PSC can consider benefits largely accruing out of state/country in a Michigan public-interest calculus.

issues.label: Authority to impose environmental conditions
issues.why: Court must decide whether PSC could/should impose environmental mitigation conditions or whether that lies with other agencies.

issues.label: Record treatment of expert testimony
issues.why: Court must ensure PSC properly evaluated competing expert evidence and explained credibility determinations.

issues.label: Disclosure of modeling assumptions
issues.why: Court must assess whether spill modeling/risk analyses were transparent and sufficiently supported for reliance.

issues.label: Tunnel engineering uncertainties
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether geotechnical risks and construction feasibility were adequately analyzed and conditioned.

issues.label: Long-term tunnel ownership risks
issues.why: Court must consider governance, inspection, and liability implications of MSCA ownership for public safety and trust resources.

issues.label: Liability/indemnification relevance
issues.why: Court must decide whether contractual indemnity/financial assurance affects the public-interest and environmental-risk evaluation.

issues.label: Financial assurance and bonding
issues.why: Court must determine whether adequate financial guarantees for construction, remediation, and abandonment were required.

issues.label: Decommissioning obligations
issues.why: Court must assess enforceability and timing of commitments to deactivate/remove the dual pipelines once replacement is operational.

issues.label: Interim operation of dual lines
issues.why: Court must consider risk management during construction while existing Straits lines continue operating.

issues.label: Consistency with state resource policies
issues.why: Court must evaluate alignment with Michigan’s natural resource protection policies and Great Lakes stewardship obligations.

issues.label: Tribal consultation adequacy
issues.why: Court must determine whether consultation duties (state or incorporated federal standards) were met regarding tribal interests.

issues.label: Cultural resources/archaeology
issues.why: Court must consider whether construction threatens cultural resources and whether review/mitigation was required.

issues.label: Navigation and commerce impacts
issues.why: Court must assess impacts to Straits navigation, fisheries, and commerce during construction and operations.

issues.label: Cumulative spill risk statewide
issues.why: Court must consider whether the decision accounted for broader spill risks along the 645-mile line within Michigan.

issues.label: Legislative intent of 2018 PA 359
issues.why: Court must interpret whether the statute’s purpose supports or limits PSC approval of the replacement segment.

issues.label: Consistency with PSC prior decisions
issues.why: Court must assess whether PSC departed from precedent without explanation in approving this project.

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and timeliness
issues.why: Court must confirm proper appellate route, deadlines, and jurisdictional prerequisites were satisfied.
